# Recordings the golden VM could not produce

Written by scripts/recorded-replies/Invoke-RecordReplies.ps1 on 2026-10-11. Each line says what is needed to record it.

- qbittorrent downloading / stalled-near-end: no peer connection formed between transmission and qbittorrent (the clients may refuse peers on one address)
- weir status-queued: the burst of hand-offs was finished before the last could be seen queued
- weir failed with failureClass not_taken (Weir #956, Deluno #1250): Weir answers it when a second connection of the same kind hands off a file whose processing pass belongs to the first; the VM has one Deluno connection to Weir, so it cannot be produced there. It needs a second processor connection in Deluno pointing at the same Weir and watched folder
- rtorrent: not installed in the VM; install it there (or on a machine the script can reach) and add a recorder
- utorrent: not installed in the VM; same
- emby, jellyfin, plex: not installed in the VM; their library, item and playback replies need a server with real media
- torznab and newznab feeds: only the golden path stubs exist in the VM, and a stub is not a real indexer; a real indexer's caps and search replies need its API key
- sabnzbd duplicate-add: SABnzbd 5.1.3 answers an addurl of a duplicate with a new job id (it fetches the NZB afterwards), so the empty-id answer was not recorded; the capture script now sends the NZB as a file (addlocalfile) for that, but it was not re-run
- qbittorrent downloading / stalled-near-end seeded by transmission: no peer connection formed; it was recorded with Deluge as the seeder
- tests not yet moved onto recordings: see tests/recorded-reply-allow-list.json (kind "pending"): only the uTorrent and rTorrent parts of eleven files, each entry saying what to record
- found while moving the tests onto recordings (#1237), replies a test needed that are not recorded; each was answered with the nearest recorded reply changed in the one value the test is about, and says so:
  - qbittorrent: the reply to torrents/setAutoManagement; the tracker list of a tracker that is not working (status 4 and its message); the reply to an add of a link (not a file) and to a link that is dead
  - deluge: the reply to core.add_torrent_url; label.* with the Label plugin switched off (the "Unknown method" error); core.get_torrent_status for a hash it never had
  - transmission: torrent-get with the fields Deluno asks for now (uploadRatio, secondsSeeding, activityDate, doneDate, seedRatioMode, seedRatioLimit, seedIdleMode, seedIdleLimit; the recording's field list was shorter); a refused torrent-set
  - sabnzbd: the history entry of a duplicate it turned down, with the wording it gives in fail_message (the recorded duplicate-add shows only the add)
  - weir: the "scheduled" state (a library with processing hours); /openapi.json; a 403 (rc.13 answers 401 for a missing and for a wrong secret); the outcome and status replies that the recordings hold for one hand-off only
  - plex, jellyfin, emby and seerr: the identity and status replies that carry their version (ConnectionVersionParserTests still holds those shapes)

## Deluno-Weir contract gaps (#1239, docs/deluno-weir-contract.md)

Recorded on 13 October 2026 (Deluno 1.0.0-rc.30.30, Weir 1.0.0-rc.13): Deluno's own requests with their headers, Weir's reports to Deluno, and Weir's refusals of a wrong secret, an unknown id, a refused body and an Origin without X-Requested-With. What is still missing:

- weir plain-text `500 Internal Server Error`, treated by Deluno as retryable: Weir has no deliberate 5xx or 429 on its intake routes. The only 5xx is the web server's plain-text 500 for an exception nothing handled (SQLite still busy after 30 s, say), and the VM cannot be made to produce that on purpose. `WeirPlainTextFiveHundredTests` builds it. `429` is never sent by Weir.
- weir `401` for a secret that belongs to a different connection than the hand-off's owner (the same text as a wrong secret): needs a second connection of the same kind in Weir with its own secret. The VM has one.
- weir `403` "Set a webhook secret in Weir so a media manager can ask about hand-offs" on the status poll was recorded under a source key with no connection (`status-no-connection-for-source`), not on Deluno's own source with its secret removed; the second needs Weir's secret for the Deluno connection to be unset, which would break the real connection.
- weir report `not_taken` (Weir #956, Deluno #1250) (listed above too): it needs a second processor connection in Deluno pointing at the same Weir and watched folder.
- weir reports `accepted`, `started` and `rejected`: in this run Weir sent only `completed` and `failed` reports to Deluno (and `source_gone` as a failure class). A `started` or `accepted` report was never sent, and `rejected` needs a reject-capable workflow.
- a report for a hand-off Deluno has no row for at all: every hand-off the reports named still had a row (a late report was answered 409 for a dismissed one). It needs a hand-off row that is gone, for example a title removed while Weir was working.
- the person's "I don't want it" on a hand-off Weir is working on (`409` working, as Deluno sent it): the cancel Deluno sent was taken while Weir still held the hand-off queued, so only the 204 is a Deluno-sent cancel. `handoff-cancel-working` and `handoff-cancel-too-late` are Weir's replies to a cancel sent by the recording script.
- weir connection refused (Weir switched off) and a timeout: no reply to record. The contract tests make the connection fail.
- weir `scheduled` and `passed-through` states on the status poll: Weir 1.0.0-rc.13 was never seen giving them. A scheduled workflow run would give `scheduled`; `passed-through` may be a state Weir no longer uses (ask the Weir session).
- weir capabilities carrying `watchedPath`: rc.13 does not send it.
- weir `outcome` for a hand-off Weir finished but whose stored note belongs to another send of the same release (#1232): the reply carried an ordinary message; a reply whose message contradicts the outcome has not been seen from the real Weir.

## GitHub (`github/2022-11-28`, #1237, #1263)

Every state is a real unauthenticated GET from the public internet, on 14 October 2026, with the user agent `Deluno-test-recording`; a recording's own note says what was asked and how it was shortened (release-note bodies and most of a long list removed). About 14 calls to `api.github.com` were spent in all, and the hourly limit was never reached.

- `weir-newest-release-has-no-files`, `nzbget-latest-release`, `release-feed-not-found`: recorded for #1263 (Weir's rc.17 was a published pre-release with no files).
- `sabnzbd-latest-release`: `api.github.com/repos/sabnzbd/sabnzbd/releases/latest`.
- `qbittorrent-tags`, `deluge-tags`: the tags API (`?per_page=100`) and `tags.atom` of two projects that tag and do not publish releases; Deluge's list carries development tags such as `deluge-2.2.1.dev0`.
- `nzbget-release-feed`: NZBGet's `releases.atom`, whose newest entry is the rolling tag `testing`, not a version.
- `weir-velopack-feed`: the `releases.win.json` file that Weir (built with Velopack) publishes beside its installer, rc.13.
- `api-not-found`: the API's own 404 body for a repository that does not exist (a private repository answers the same).
- not recorded: the anonymous rate-limit reply (a 403 or 429 with `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`) and a bare 503. Recording the limit would mean using the whole hourly allowance of a shared address, so tests of those states build the status and its `X-RateLimit-*` / `Retry-After` headers by hand (no body of an app's shape is involved). `jampat000/Deluno` has no public release feed yet, so Deluno's own update feed is tested with Weir's, which is built the same way.
- states a test needs that GitHub was not in (the newest release a draft, a release changed into a stable one, the feed listed oldest first) are the nearest recorded reply with only that value changed, and each test says so.

### Reports Weir sends Deluno that the tests still build inline (#1239, needs a Weir re-record on the golden VM)

Deluno's own replies to the calls Weir makes are now recorded (`deluno/1.0.0-rc.30.32/reply-*`, from the server code, see `docs/deluno-weir-contract.md` section 9). The reports Weir sends to `POST /api/integrations/processors/events` are the real Weir's wherever one was recorded (`deluno/1.0.0-rc.30.30/events-*`): `ProcessorCallbackContractTests`, `AProcessorIsNotTakenAtItsWordTests`, `ALateReportForARemovedSendIsSettledTests` and `AResentReleaseSettlesItsOwnHandOffTests` post those bodies (through `RecordedWeirReports`) for a finished single file, release folder and Usenet job, a report after the person stopped waiting, and the held, unreadable and source-gone failures. The cases below have no real Weir report, so their bodies stay inline in those four classes, each marked "deliberate" here with the Weir state that would produce it. `scripts/check-recorded-replies.mjs` does not see them (it recognises another app's reply, and these are requests to Deluno), so they need no allow-list entry.

- `accepted` and `started` reports (DELIBERATE and never to be recorded: the generic processor contract allows a processor to send them, but Weir never does. Its push statuses are only `completed` and `failed`; "accepted" is Deluno's own 2xx answer to a hand-off and "started" is the status poll saying `working`) (`A_report_may_list_exactly_the_maximum_number_of_files`, `A_report_repeated_for_a_hand_off_already_started_is_accepted_again...`): these two stay inline for good, each test marked deliberate for that reason.
- `failed` with `disposition: "rejected"` and `sourceRemoved: true` (`A_failed_report_for_a_removed_send_that_was_asked_for_again_is_settled_too`, the `rejected` case): needs a Weir workflow with a reject rule (a release type it throws away), so that a download is rejected rather than held.
- `failed` carrying `outputFiles` and a `message` that counts what failed, with or without `outputPath` (`A_partial_failure_imports_what_succeeded...`, `A_small_extra_the_processor_left_out...`, `A_failed_report_that_names_its_output_files_but_no_output_path...`, `A_main_video_the_processor_failed_still_fails_the_hand_off`, `A_later_failed_report_for_one_small_extra...`): needs a release folder that holds a film plus a featurette under Weir's 50 MB minimum, and a TV season pack where one episode fails; the recorded failures all carry an empty `outputFiles`.
- `completed` for a TV season pack naming several episodes in `outputFiles` and a folder `outputPath` (`A_folder_hand_off_with_several_output_files_imports_as_one_pack`, `Output_files_the_processor_names_but_are_not_there_are_reported`): needs a TV library on the golden VM and a season-pack hand-off; the recorded folders hold one film.
- `completed` from an older Weir with no `outputFiles` (`A_completion_with_no_output_files_from_an_older_processor_still_works`): current Weir always sends it, so this one is a deliberate old-shape case.
- `completed` that names a file belonging to another hand-off, or a path outside the library's output folder (`A_file_that_is_another_downloads...`, `...claimed_by_another_hand_off...`, `An_output_path_outside_the_configured_folder...`, `A_file_that_names_no_download_at_all...`): needs a Weir whose output folder or path mapping disagrees with Deluno's, so that the path it reports is outside Deluno's.
- the same `completed` report twice (`The_same_completion_reported_twice_imports_once`, `A_second_completion_of_a_completed_hand_off...` second post, `The_first_sends_late_completed_report_with_its_output...`): the first post is Weir's recorded body; the repeat is Weir resending after it did not hear Deluno (Deluno restarted or answered 5xx). Needs Deluno switched off while Weir reports, so Weir's own retry arrives.
- a report that lists more than 1000 files or a path over 4096 characters, a status word Deluno does not know (`halfway`), a `completed` with no `outputPath`, a report for a library Deluno does not have (the `400` cases): Weir never sends these, so they are deliberate hand-built limits and are not expected to be recorded.
- `401`, `403` and `429` for the events route (`No_sign_in_is_401_and_a_key_without_the_imports_scope_is_403`): Deluno's own replies to a missing credential and a key without the scope are recorded for the four routes in `reply-no-sign-in` and `reply-key-without-imports-scope`; what Weir does on receiving them needs a Weir whose Deluno API key is wrong or lacks the scope (a Weir-side recording). `429` needs more than 3000 requests a minute from one key and is not expected.
- the library-wide `download-destinations` reply with a routed download client (`destinations[]` filled): the recordings hold a library with no client routed, because the test host cannot ask a real client. It needs the golden VM's Deluno asked while a qBittorrent, a SABnzbd and a Transmission are routed to a library.

## Processor output layout (#1262)

`AProcessorsFinishedFileIsFoundWhereItPutItTests` uses Weir 1.0.0-rc.13's recorded replies for a flat single file, a file in a release folder, a folder hand-off and a resend whose finished status has no `outputPath` (`resend-status-completed`). Two layouts have no real Weir reply behind them yet:

- weir `stem (n).ext` name collision: the file the test puts in the output folder is named by the layout rule in Weir's source (`RemuxPublish.cs`), not by a reply. Produce it on the golden VM by handing Weir two different single files with the same file name one after the other (the first left in the output folder), then record the second hand-off's completed status and its `completed` report.
- weir completed status with no `outputPath` after a takeover, a finished hand-off id received again, or a hand-off settled as cancelled (Weir rc.14 and later clear the path): rc.13 was the build on the VM and never gave them. After the VM runs Weir rc.14 or later, resend a finished single-file hand-off with takeover and record the status poll and the report. Until then the resend after a takeover is covered by the same null-path shape as `resend-status-completed` and `status-cancelled`.

## Planned for the Weir 1.0.0-rc.18 recording (one run, `Invoke-RecordReplies.ps1 -Extra weir-states,weir-reports,weir-errors -IncludeBaseWeir`)

Every state below is made on the golden VM by `scripts/recorded-replies/Record-WeirReports.ps1` (the reports, through a proxy that Weir's connection to Deluno is pointed at for the run and put back after) and `Record-WeirErrors.ps1` (the two server errors, on a second Weir server made for the purpose). Until that run is made these lines stay open; when it has been, each is replaced by the recording's name or by what the run could not produce.

- `weir/1.0.0-rc.18`: `resend-takeover-*` (a single file sent twice at once; the second send's final status should be completed with no `outputPath`), `output-collision-replace-*` and `output-collision-keep-both-*` (two different single files with one name, one after the other, the first left in the output folder; Weir renames only under the `keep_both` policy, and its source numbers from (2), see `OutputCollision.NextFreePath`, so a `stem (1).ext` may not be seen: the recording says what the output folder held), `failed-rejected-status`, `completed-season-pack-status-*`, `failed-partial-season-pack-*`.
- `deluno/<version>`: `events-superseded`, `events-completed-after-takeover`, `events-completed-collision-*`, `events-failed-rejected` (an audio-only .mkv under the `reject` failure policy; Deluno advertises `processor-reject-regrab`), `events-completed-season-pack`, `events-failed-partial-season-pack` (a season folder with one corrupt episode under the `hold` policy), `events-completed-repeated-after-503` (the proxy answers the first POST 503; Weir sends it again on its next one-minute heartbeat), `events-answered-401-not-repeated` and `events-answered-403-not-repeated` (the proxy answers once; the recording shows how many more POSTs came in the following 130 s). The hand-offs are made straight to Weir, so Deluno has no row for them: where the proxy forwards a report to real Deluno its answer is a 409 for an unknown hand-off, not the 202 of a known one, and each note says what Deluno said and what the proxy told Weir.
- `weir/1.0.0-rc.18`: `database-busy-outcome`, `database-busy-handoff`, `database-busy-retried` (another program holds the database's write lock longer than `WEIR_SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`; Weir's own contract tests do it with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on its SQLite file) and `internal-error-outcome` (a table the route reads is missing; its contract test drops `media_manager_handoffs`). Neither can be made on the Weir the VM is using without breaking it, so both are made on a second Weir server started from the installed one with its own data folder, a one-second busy timeout and its own webhook secret. The lock is held through `winsqlite3.dll`, which Windows ships. A `503` for a hand-off needs a Weir library to exist, which the second server has none of, so `database-busy-handoff` is recorded only if Weir answers 503 before it checks the library; if not, it is listed here as not produced.

### The 14 October 2026 attempt captured nothing (read this before the next run)

The first run against a VM with Weir 1.0.0-rc.18 was stopped by the owner during the base Weir states, before the host had received anything (the host only gets a run's recordings when the whole run ends), so **no `weir/1.0.0-rc.18` or `deluno/1.0.0-rc.30.32` recording exists yet and every state in the section above is still to be produced**. It did find, and the scripts now handle:

- `Save-State` also writes each recording to `C:\golden\recorded\saved-states.jsonl` in the VM as it is made; a stopped run is recovered by copying that file out and running `scripts/recorded-replies/Import-SavedStates.ps1 -File <it> -Name <vm name>`.
- Weir rc.18 takes each workflow's watched folder from Deluno about a minute after the workflow is saved, and refuses a hand-off sent sooner ("No Weir workflow watches the folder ..."). `Initialize-Environment.ps1` now waits for it; a scenario or recording started before that fails for no product reason.
- `-Extra` takes a list only through `-Command`: `powershell -Command "& .\scripts\recorded-replies\Invoke-RecordReplies.ps1 -RigHost <host> -VmName <vm> -Apps weir -Extra weir-states,weir-reports,weir-errors -IncludeBaseWeir -DelunoVersion <v> -WeirVersion 1.0.0-rc.18 -VmMediaFile <film>"` (with `-File` the commas make one string and the parameter check refuses it).
- A VM set up by the suite's `Initialize-SuiteEnvironment` is required (the reports recorder signs in with the suite's throwaway Weir login). Use the 362 MB `C:\golden\suite\base\big\...mkv` as `-VmMediaFile`; it keeps Weir busy long enough for a takeover.
- The base `completed-without-output-path` state was again not produced on rc.18 by sending one source twice at once (the second send finished with an output path), which is why `Record-WeirReports.ps1` records the takeover with a big film and names what happened.
- `resend.single-file.takeover` ran once (15.8 min, failed): the first hand-off was refused by the watched-folder race above, so none of its checks about Weir's answer or Deluno's import were reached. It has not passed yet.
